manifest.title: Formal Tree Bounds for the Sum Network Creation Game

inputs.abstract:
In the sum network creation game, each player pays a price $\alpha$ per edge
it purchases and the sum of its undirected distances to all other players.
An unreachable vertex contributes infinite distance. A Nash equilibrium is
stable under unilateral changes to the entire purchased edge set.

This development formalizes Dippel and Vetta's general tree theorem at
$\alpha>2n$. It proves that an equilibrium at $\alpha>n$ has girth at least
eight and that it is a tree for up to ten players. It also checks an improved
deletion bound for purchases into degree-two vertices of maximal cyclic
blocks, and a weighted addition inequality for block attachments.

The formal game definitions adapt the Apache-2.0 sources of
[lax-899194](https://laxarchive.org/lax-899194/index.html), originally developed
in [the upstream repository](https://github.com/clemenskuske/network-creation-tree-equilibria/tree/ab7c839f02a08a417dcf6ccbf6f447790ddd5db3).
The archive package changes the namespace and adds mathematical definitions
and proofs. OpenAI Codex assisted in developing and documenting the Lean
proofs and their computational certificates.

The full Tree Conjecture for all player counts at $\alpha>n$ is open in this
development. The attached repository also records mathematical arguments
with external integer checks for additive refinements of the general bound.

concepts.title: Maximal biconnected blocks and their attachment weights
concepts.description:
A block is a maximal vertex set of size at least three that stays connected
after removal of any one vertex. The block graph is induced on that set
and retains the ambient vertex type. The attachment of a block vertex $v$
contains each player with a walk whose first entry into the block is $v$.
Its weight is the cardinality of that attachment.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Metric
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Powerset

/-!
---
title: Maximal biconnected blocks and their attachment weights
type: definition
---
A block is a maximal vertex set of size at least three that stays connected
after removal of any one vertex. The block graph is induced on that set
and retains the ambient vertex type. The attachment of a block vertex $v$
contains each player with a walk whose first entry into the block is $v$.
Its weight is the cardinality of that attachment.
-/

namespace Lax869952.BlockGeometry

variable {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}

/-- The induced two-connected vertex set, expressed in ambient walks. -/
structure TwoConnectedOn (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Finset V) : Prop where
  card_ge_three : 3 ≤ S.card
  walk (z : V) {x y : V} (hx : x ∈ S) (hy : y ∈ S) (hxz : x ≠ z) (hyz : y ≠ z) :
    ∃ p : G.Walk x y, (∀ a ∈ p.support, a ∈ S) ∧ z ∉ p.support

/-- Maximality excludes bridge blocks. -/
structure IsBiconnectedBlock (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Finset V) : Prop where
  twoConnected : TwoConnectedOn G S
  maximal (T : Finset V) : S ⊆ T → TwoConnectedOn G T → T ⊆ S

def blockGraph (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Finset V) : SimpleGraph V :=
  ((⊤ : G.Subgraph).induce (↑S : Set V)).spanningCoe

def FirstEntryInto (S : Finset V) {x y : V} (p : G.Walk x y) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ p.support, a ∈ S → a = y

noncomputable def blockAttachment {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) (v : Fin n) : Finset (Fin n) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter (fun x => ∃ p : G.Walk x v, FirstEntryInto S p)

end Lax869952.BlockGeometry

concepts.title: Girth at least eight at price above the player count
concepts.description: At $\alpha>n$, every cycle in a pure Nash equilibrium has at least eight edges.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Metric

/-!
---
title: Girth at least eight at price above the player count
type: theorem
---
At $\alpha>n$, every cycle in a pure Nash equilibrium has at least eight edges.
-/

namespace Lax869952.GirthAtPopulationPrice

open Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
open scoped NNReal BigOperators

axiom statement {n : ℕ} (s : Profile n) (α : ℝ≥0)
    (hα : (n : ℝ≥0) < α) (hne : IsNashEquilibrium α s)
    {u : Fin n} (p : (graph s).Walk u u) (hp : p.IsCycle) : 8 ≤ p.length

end Lax869952.GirthAtPopulationPrice

statements.signature:
statement : ∀ {n : Nat} (s : Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.Profile n) (α : NNReal),
  NNReal.instPartialOrder.lt n.cast α →
    Lax869952.NashEquilibrium.IsNashEquilibrium α s →
      ∀ {u : Fin n} (p : (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s).Walk u u), p.IsCycle → instLENat.le 8 p.length

concepts.title: Weighted leaf addition inequality for a maximal block
concepts.description: If a block vertex $v$ has another player in its attachment, its attachment and the block distances satisfy every single-addition inequality of a leaf at $v$. The weights are actual attachment cardinalities.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
import Lax869952.BlockGeometry

/-!
---
title: Weighted leaf addition inequality for a maximal block
type: theorem
---
If a block vertex $v$ has another player in its attachment, its attachment and the block distances satisfy every single-addition inequality of a leaf at $v$. The weights are actual attachment cardinalities.
-/

namespace Lax869952.LeafAdditionInequality

open Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
open scoped NNReal BigOperators

axiom statement {n : ℕ} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (α : ℝ≥0) (s : Profile n)
    (hne : IsNashEquilibrium α s) (hS : BlockGeometry.IsBiconnectedBlock (graph s) S)
    {v r : Fin n} (hv : v ∈ S) (hr : r ∈ S) (hvr : v ≠ r)
    (hWeight : 1 < (BlockGeometry.blockAttachment (graph s) S v).card) :
    (∑ z ∈ S, ((BlockGeometry.blockAttachment (graph s) S z).card : ℝ) *
      max 0 (((BlockGeometry.blockGraph (graph s) S).dist v z : ℝ) -
        ((BlockGeometry.blockGraph (graph s) S).dist r z : ℝ))) ≤ (α : ℝ)

end Lax869952.LeafAdditionInequality

statements.signature:
statement : ∀ {n : Nat} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (α : NNReal) (s : Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.Profile n),
  Lax869952.NashEquilibrium.IsNashEquilibrium α s →
    Lax869952.BlockGeometry.IsBiconnectedBlock (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S →
      ∀ {v r : Fin n},
        SetLike.instMembership.mem S v →
          SetLike.instMembership.mem S r →
            Ne v r →
              instLTNat.lt 1
                  (Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockAttachment (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S v).card →
                Real.instLE.le
                  (S.sum fun z =>
                    instHMul.hMul
                      (Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockAttachment (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S z).card.cast
                      (Real.instMax.max 0
                        (instHSub.hSub
                          ((Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockGraph (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S).dist v z).cast
                          ((Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockGraph (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S).dist r
                              z).cast)))
                  α.toReal

concepts.title: Pure Nash equilibrium
concepts.description:
A strategy profile is a pure Nash equilibrium when no player can reduce its
individual cost by changing its own strategy while all other players keep
their strategies. A deviation may replace the entire set of purchased edges.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The comparison is between costs in the two resulting networks, including
deviations that disconnect the network. Equality is allowed, so weak and
transient equilibria are included.

The displayed equilibrium inequality on p. 348 of the paper has its direction
reversed. We use cost minimization, as specified by the surrounding discussion
and explicitly by footnote 4 on p. 350: the current cost is at most the cost
after any unilateral deviation.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax869952.PlayerCost

/-!
---
title: Pure Nash equilibrium
type: definition
---
A strategy profile is a pure Nash equilibrium when no player can reduce its
individual cost by changing its own strategy while all other players keep
their strategies. A deviation may replace the entire set of purchased edges.

# Formalization notes

The comparison is between costs in the two resulting networks, including
deviations that disconnect the network. Equality is allowed, so weak and
transient equilibria are included.

The displayed equilibrium inequality on p. 348 of the paper has its direction
reversed. We use cost minimization, as specified by the surrounding discussion
and explicitly by footnote 4 on p. 350: the current cost is at most the cost
after any unilateral deviation.
-/

namespace Lax869952.NashEquilibrium

open Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame Lax869952.PlayerCost
open scoped NNReal

/-- No unilateral replacement of a player's strategy lowers that player's cost. -/
def IsNashEquilibrium {n : ℕ} (α : ℝ≥0) (s : Profile n) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Fin n) (t : Profile n),
    (∀ j : Fin n, j ≠ i → t j = s j) →
      playerCost α s i ≤ playerCost α t i

end Lax869952.NashEquilibrium

concepts.title: Network creation game
concepts.description:
There are $n$ players, indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. A strategy of player
$i$ is a set $s_i$ of other players: player $i$ purchases an edge to each member
of $s_i$. A strategy profile specifies one strategy for every player.

The resulting network $G[s]$ is undirected. Distinct players $i$ and $j$ are
adjacent when $j\in s_i$ or $i\in s_j$. Either endpoint may purchase an edge,
and both endpoints may purchase the same edge.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Strategies are subsets of `Fin n`, with self-purchases excluded by their type.
Every such subset is finite. Edge ownership remains part of the profile even
though the resulting graph is a simple graph.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card

/-!
---
title: Network creation game
type: definition
---
There are $n$ players, indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. A strategy of player
$i$ is a set $s_i$ of other players: player $i$ purchases an edge to each member
of $s_i$. A strategy profile specifies one strategy for every player.

The resulting network $G[s]$ is undirected. Distinct players $i$ and $j$ are
adjacent when $j\in s_i$ or $i\in s_j$. Either endpoint may purchase an edge,
and both endpoints may purchase the same edge.

# Formalization notes

Strategies are subsets of `Fin n`, with self-purchases excluded by their type.
Every such subset is finite. Edge ownership remains part of the profile even
though the resulting graph is a simple graph.
-/

namespace Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame

/-- The other players to which player `i` purchases edges. -/
def Strategy (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) := { S : Set (Fin n) // i ∉ S }

/-- A choice of strategy for every player. -/
abbrev Profile (n : ℕ) := (i : Fin n) → Strategy n i

/-- The undirected network formed by all purchased edges. -/
def graph {n : ℕ} (s : Profile n) : SimpleGraph (Fin n) where
  Adj i j := j ∈ (s i).val ∨ i ∈ (s j).val
  symm := ⟨fun _ _ h => h.elim Or.inr Or.inl⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun i h => h.elim (s i).property (s i).property⟩

end Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame

concepts.title: Individual cost in the network creation game
concepts.description:
For an edge price $\alpha>0$, player $i$ has cost
$c_i(s)=\alpha|s_i|+\sum_j d_{G[s]}(i,j)$.
The distance is the length of a shortest path, and is infinite if there is no
path. A player pays for every edge it purchases, including an edge also
purchased by its other endpoint.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Costs take values in the extended nonnegative reals so that disconnected
networks retain the infinite penalty. `SimpleGraph.edist` supplies the graph
distance, and `ENat.toENNReal` preserves both finite distances and infinity.
The edge price is a finite nonnegative real; the theorem assumes it is positive.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Metric
import Mathlib.Data.Real.ENatENNReal
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Defs

/-!
---
title: Individual cost in the network creation game
type: definition
---
For an edge price $\alpha>0$, player $i$ has cost
$c_i(s)=\alpha|s_i|+\sum_j d_{G[s]}(i,j)$.
The distance is the length of a shortest path, and is infinite if there is no
path. A player pays for every edge it purchases, including an edge also
purchased by its other endpoint.

# Formalization notes

Costs take values in the extended nonnegative reals so that disconnected
networks retain the infinite penalty. `SimpleGraph.edist` supplies the graph
distance, and `ENat.toENNReal` preserves both finite distances and infinity.
The edge price is a finite nonnegative real; the theorem assumes it is positive.
-/

namespace Lax869952.PlayerCost

open Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame
open scoped BigOperators NNReal ENNReal

/-- Edge expenditure plus the sum of distances from player `i` to all players. -/
noncomputable def playerCost {n : ℕ} (α : ℝ≥0) (s : Profile n)
    (i : Fin n) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  (α : ℝ≥0∞) * (s i).val.ncard +
    ∑ j : Fin n, ((graph s).edist i j).toENNReal

end Lax869952.PlayerCost

concepts.title: Deletion bound for a purchase into a degree-two block vertex
concepts.description:
Let $v$ have degree two in a maximal cyclic block of a Nash equilibrium of girth at least eight. If a neighbor buys an edge into $v$, then for any cycle of length $c$ through $v$ in that block, the attachment weight $w(v)$ satisfies

$$\alpha+6\le 2(c-3)w(v).$$

The result allows either owner of the other edge incident to $v$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
import Lax869952.BlockGeometry

/-!
---
title: Deletion bound for a purchase into a degree-two block vertex
type: theorem
---
Let $v$ have degree two in a maximal cyclic block of a Nash equilibrium of girth at least eight. If a neighbor buys an edge into $v$, then for any cycle of length $c$ through $v$ in that block, the attachment weight $w(v)$ satisfies

$$\alpha+6\le 2(c-3)w(v).$$

The result allows either owner of the other edge incident to $v$.
-/

namespace Lax869952.ReceiverDeletionBound

open Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
open scoped NNReal BigOperators

axiom statement {n : ℕ} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (s : Profile n) (α : ℝ≥0)
    (hne : IsNashEquilibrium α s) (hS : BlockGeometry.IsBiconnectedBlock (graph s) S)
    [DecidableRel (BlockGeometry.blockGraph (graph s) S).Adj]
    (girth : ∀ {x}, (p : (graph s).Walk x x) → p.IsCycle → 8 ≤ p.length)
    {u v w : Fin n} (huv : (BlockGeometry.blockGraph (graph s) S).Adj u v)
    (hvw : (BlockGeometry.blockGraph (graph s) S).Adj v w) (huw : u ≠ w)
    (hdegree : (BlockGeometry.blockGraph (graph s) S).degree v = 2)
    (hBuy : v ∈ (s u).val)
    (c : (BlockGeometry.blockGraph (graph s) S).Walk v v) (hc : c.IsCycle) :
    (α : ℝ) + 6 ≤ 2 * ((c.length : ℝ) - 3) *
      ((BlockGeometry.blockAttachment (graph s) S v).card : ℝ)

end Lax869952.ReceiverDeletionBound

statements.signature:
statement : ∀ {n : Nat} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (s : Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.Profile n) (α : NNReal),
  Lax869952.NashEquilibrium.IsNashEquilibrium α s →
    Lax869952.BlockGeometry.IsBiconnectedBlock (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S →
      ∀ [inst : DecidableRel (Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockGraph (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S).Adj],
        (∀ {x : Fin n} (p : (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s).Walk x x), p.IsCycle → instLENat.le 8 p.length) →
          ∀ {u v w : Fin n},
            (Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockGraph (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S).Adj u v →
              (Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockGraph (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S).Adj v w →
                Ne u w →
                  Eq ((Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockGraph (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S).degree v) 2 →
                    Set.instMembership.mem (s u).val v →
                      ∀ (c : (Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockGraph (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S).Walk v v),
                        c.IsCycle →
                          Real.instLE.le (instHAdd.hAdd α.toReal 6)
                            (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 2 (instHSub.hSub c.length.cast 3))
                              (Lax869952.BlockGeometry.blockAttachment (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s) S
                                    v).card.cast)

concepts.title: The Tree Conjecture for up to ten players
concepts.description: For $1\le n\le10$ and $\alpha>n$, every pure Nash equilibrium graph is a tree.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic

/-!
---
title: The Tree Conjecture for up to ten players
type: theorem
---
For $1\le n\le10$ and $\alpha>n$, every pure Nash equilibrium graph is a tree.
-/

namespace Lax869952.SmallGames

open Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
open scoped NNReal BigOperators

axiom statement {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hsmall : n ≤ 10)
    (s : Profile n) (α : ℝ≥0) (hα : (n : ℝ≥0) < α)
    (hne : IsNashEquilibrium α s) : (graph s).IsTree

end Lax869952.SmallGames

statements.signature:
statement : ∀ {n : Nat},
  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    instLENat.le n 10 →
      ∀ (s : Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.Profile n) (α : NNReal),
        NNReal.instPartialOrder.lt n.cast α →
          Lax869952.NashEquilibrium.IsNashEquilibrium α s → (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s).IsTree

concepts.title: Tree equilibria above twice the player count
concepts.description: On a positive number of players, an edge price $\alpha>2n$ forces every pure Nash equilibrium graph to be a tree. This is the theorem of Dippel and Vetta (STACS 2024, Theorem 1).
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic

/-!
---
title: Tree equilibria above twice the player count
type: theorem
---
On a positive number of players, an edge price $\alpha>2n$ forces every pure Nash equilibrium graph to be a tree. This is the theorem of Dippel and Vetta (STACS 2024, Theorem 1).
-/

namespace Lax869952.TreeAtDoublePrice

open Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame Lax869952.NashEquilibrium
open scoped NNReal BigOperators

axiom statement {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (α : ℝ≥0) (hα : 2 * (n : ℝ≥0) < α)
    (s : Profile n) (hne : IsNashEquilibrium α s) : (graph s).IsTree

end Lax869952.TreeAtDoublePrice

statements.signature:
statement : ∀ {n : Nat},
  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    ∀ (α : NNReal),
      NNReal.instPartialOrder.lt (instHMul.hMul 2 n.cast) α →
        ∀ (s : Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.Profile n),
          Lax869952.NashEquilibrium.IsNashEquilibrium α s → (Lax869952.NetworkCreationGame.graph s).IsTree

proofs.description: After excluding triangles and squares, use the certificates for isometric cycles of length five, six and seven. Lean checks the normalized distance labels, orientation coverage and weighted deviation inequalities. Any shortest cycle of the equilibrium graph is isometric.

Choose a player outside the block attached at $v$. A link from that player to $r$ saves at least the positive part of the difference in block distances for each destination. Nash equilibrium bounds the sum of these savings by the edge price.
Compare the equal-cost swap past the receiver with deletion of the edge. Two destinations on the complementary cycle arc improve the standard deletion estimate by two and four units, respectively.

The argument passes to a cyclic maximal biconnected block and a compatible shortest-path tree. Layered deviations bound the repeated purchase incidences and the resulting count contradicts the block degree sum.
In a cyclic block at the stated price, some vertex has block degree at least three. The girth-eight condition then requires at least eleven block vertices.
